title: When can a lithium-ion cell design search trust a reduced battery model (SPMe) instead of the full DFN model?
lede: research programme on fidelity-aware Li-ion electrode design; milestone 7f: with a margin chosen by nested leave-one-pool-out, simulating only drift-flagged designs to cycle 50 meets the held-out tail-error target on 9 to 10 of 12 design pools at 20% fewer PyBaMM DFN cycles than running every design to 50; a uniform run length with the same margin saves nothing
summary:
Milestone 7f (an out-of-batch margin): 7e's triage policy, chosen on two design pools, met the third pool's target in 4 of 12 folds. With the margin chosen by nested leave-one-pool-out, an absolute threshold on the drift score meets 9 of 12 and a flag fraction 10 of 12, both at 40.0 DFN cycles per design against 50 for all-50 (20% saved); the uniform rule's margin always lands on 50 cycles (12 of 12, 0% saved), and widening the flagged fraction alone meets 6. Limits: 8 to 12 designs per pool, the drift score's fit saw every pool, no fresh fourth pool yet. Milestone 7e (the triage frontier): over tail-error targets of 1.00 to 2.00 times the all-50-cycle upper quartile, flagging designs by 7c's ten-cycle drift score and extending only those saves 55%, 61%, 33% and 46% of the all-50 DFN cycles on Ai2020, Chen2020, OKane2022 and NCA_Kim2011 (uniform run lengths 36%, 39%, 27%, 18%; random flags 48%, 52%, 30%, 31%), chosen in hindsight within each set. A 30-cycle extension cannot reach 1.25 times the 50-cycle tail on three sets. Picked on two design pools and applied to the third, the policy met the target in 4 of 12 folds (uniform 7 of 12), so the savings are an in-sample ceiling. H273 and H275 supported, H274 and H276 refuted. Milestone 7d (flag and extend): the real ten-cycle forecast of cycle-99 lithium loss misses by 11.4% at the upper quartile on Chen2020 (5.7% with a 50-cycle line). Extending to cycle 50 only the designs 7c's ten-cycle drift score flags meets 1.25 times the all-50 tail error with 15% of designs extended (68% of the DFN cycles saved; random flags 40%), and on NCA_Kim2011 with 45% (44% against 20%); on OKane2022 no score, not even a hindsight oracle, saves much (85% to 95% extended). With every input measured, cycle-2 plating depth alone flags best on LG M50 (64% saved). Pre-registered: H269, H271, H272 supported, H270 inconclusive. Milestone 7c (the per-design drift): with every input measured, each LG M50 design's fade-law drift over cycles 10 to 99 tracks the plating-weighted depth at cycle 2 (Spearman ρ = 0.80 on Chen2020 and OKane2022, Holm p = 0.0003; plating nearer the separator speeds the rate up). A leave-one-out correction on it leaves the set-median cycle-99 lithium-loss error near 2% (typical drift 4%, about the correction's own error) but, post hoc, halves the upper quartile (8.0% to 3.5%, 7.3% to 3.0%); on the real ten-cycle forecast it beats the line on all four sets. H265, H268 supported, H266 refuted, H267 inconclusive. Milestone 7b (the law floor): with every input measured, the set-median cycle-99 lithium-loss error on LG M50 moves only from 1.8% to 1.6% (Chen2020) and 1.9% to 1.4% (OKane2022) as the law's line window grows from 10 to 50 cycles, while the real ten-cycle forecast falls from 5.6% to 2.7% and 6.7% to 2.1%: longer windows fix the inputs, not the law. The measured R(L) is linear in cycle number at the set median but drifts ±5 to 10% by design, so a borrowed curvature hurts; on Ai2020, whose R accelerates on every design, it cuts the floor from 8.3% to 4.8%. H261 supported, H263 inconclusive, H260, H262, H264 refuted. Milestone 7a (held-out error budget, the paper's table): 5zu's Shapley split of the ten-cycle lithium-plating forecast error, repeated on 64 PyBaMM DFN designs no earlier step used, keeps every direction: the anode OCP rise is the largest input on OKane2022 and NCA_Kim2011, the drift on Chen2020, the capacity factor adds nothing, and on Ai2020 measuring the inputs makes the forecast worse (2.9% to 8.3%). But with all inputs measured the forecast still misses cycle-99 lithium loss by 3.4% on OKane2022 and 3.2% on Chen2020 (1.5% and 1.4% in sample), so out of sample over half the LG M50 error is the law's ten-cycle line. H256 to H259 supported. Milestone 5zz (second fresh pool): on 32 more PyBaMM DFN designs, the per-node anode thickness line, fitted on all 72 earlier designs and used only inside their thickness range, beats the uniform node lever's set-median cycle-99 lithium-loss error on NCA_Kim2011 only (5.3% to 3.7%) and is worse on Ai2020 (1.2% to 3.4%), Chen2020 and OKane2022 (5.1% to 6.2%); it wins 14 of 29 in-range designs and 33 of 64 over both fresh pools. The design's own measured anode OCP rise beats the uniform lever on only 14 of 32, so outside NCA_Kim2011 the lever is not the forecast's limit. H254 supported; H252, H253, H255 refuted. Milestone 5zy (held-out node gains): node-gain profiles learned on 5zk's 40 designs, applied to 32 fresh PyBaMM DFN designs (8 per set, run to 100 cycles), still read the cycle-99 anode OCP rise better than the uniform lever on every set; the per-node thickness line has the lowest set-median ten-cycle lithium-loss error on three of four sets (OKane2022 7.2% to 5.6%, Chen2020 7.5% to 6.5%, NCA_Kim2011 3.3% to 2.5%; Ai2020 4.4% to 5.0%) but beats the uniform lever on only 19 of 32 designs, missing two thin OKane2022 designs by 14 to 15%. The pre-registered monotonicity gate fired on NCA_Kim2011 only. H248 and H251 supported, H249 and H250 inconclusive. Milestone 5zx (design-matched node gains): taking the borrowed late node-gain profile from the three nearest designs in design space (leave one design out, 40 PyBaMM DFN designs) keeps OKane2022's cycle-99 lithium-loss forecast at 4.5% error (uniform lever 6.7%) but leaves Chen2020 (6.5% against 5.4%) and NCA_Kim2011 (4.1% against 3.0%) worse, no better than 5zw's set median; the neighbours sit 0.6 to 0.75 of the design cube apart. A per-node line in anode thickness, reported after the plan, reaches 2.7% on OKane2022 and 1.5% on NCA_Kim2011, at or below the measured-OCP ceiling, and fails on Ai2020 and Chen2020, where the separator node's late gain is not monotone in thickness. Pre-registered H246 supported, H244 and H245 refuted, H247 inconclusive. Milestone 5zw (node-gain transfer): carrying the median per-node gain profile of the other designs in a set (leave one design out, 40 PyBaMM DFN designs) takes the ten-cycle forecast of cycle-99 lithium loss on OKane2022 from 6.7% to 4.1% error (the measured-OCP ceiling is 3.5%) and reads the anode OCP rise better than the uniform lever on all four sets, but Chen2020 (5.4% to 6.5%) and NCA_Kim2011 (3.0% to 4.2%) get worse and only 23 of 40 designs improve. Milestone 5zv (per-node gains): a gain per anode node on the node lever's uniform stoichiometry shift, fitted over cycles 3 to 10 of 40 PyBaMM DFN designs, takes the cycle-99 lithium-loss forecast on Chen2020 from 5.4% to 3.9% (the measured-OCP ceiling) and on NCA_Kim2011 from 3.0% to 2.3%, but on OKane2022 its gains (0.1 to 0.8) over-correct and the forecast stays at 6.9% against 6.7%; 22 of 40 designs improve, and gains on the separator-side nodes only (found after the plan) are a lead at 4.1%, on 6 of 12 designs. Milestone 5zu (the error budget): scoring all eight forecast-or-measured combinations of the node lever's OCP rise, the non-OCP plating-overpotential drift and the charge-capacity factor on 40 PyBaMM DFN designs, a Shapley split gives the OCP rise 3.3 of the 5.6 points between the ten-cycle forecast and the all-measured diagnosis on OKane2022 (drift 1.1), the two 2.1 and 2.0 on Chen2020, and the factor under 0.3 on every set; on Ai2020 measuring the inputs makes the forecast worse (2.3% to 8.0%). Milestone 5zt (the drift tie): tying the non-OCP drift of the plating-weighted plating overpotential to the falling charge overpotential forecasts its cycle-99 value in 40 PyBaMM DFN designs within 3.5 to 6.0 mV (a ten-cycle line: 7.1 to 13.0), but added to the node lever it worsens the cycle-99 lithium-loss forecast on all four sets (7.6% against 5.4% on Chen2020) and beats the law's lever on 17 of 40 designs; the measured drift takes Chen2020 to 2.4% but leaves OKane2022 at 6.5%. Milestone 5zs (the capacity factor is done): a saturating ten-cycle fit of the charge overpotential in the electrode-balance window forecasts the cycle-99 charge-capacity factor of 40 PyBaMM DFN designs within 2.4 to 4.8% on all four sets (a ten-cycle line: 3.6 to 7.6%), and the node lever fed the measured factor itself changes its cycle-99 lithium-loss error by at most 0.7 points on three sets; with the saturating factor the node lever beats the law's own lever on 22 of 40 designs. The remaining ten-cycle error on LG M50 (5.4 to 7.6%) is the plating-overpotential lever. Milestone 5zr (the capacity factor is the electrode balance): the open-circuit electrode-balance window with a ten-cycle line in the charge overpotential forecasts the cycle-99 charge-capacity factor of 40 PyBaMM DFN designs within 3.6 to 7.6% on all four sets, where a straight line missed by 16 to 51%, and the law's own factor is within 2.4 to 7.1%; the effective charge overpotential falls by 6 to 18 mV over ten cycles rather than growing. Fed to the forecast law with the node lever it beats the law's own lever on 14 of 40 designs and is no better than the node lever alone, so the remaining ten-cycle error on LG M50 is the lever. Milestone 5zq (ten-cycle forecasts of the two inputs): extrapolating the non-OCP plating overpotential drift and the charge-capacity factor from cycles 2..10 of 40 PyBaMM DFN designs, the forecast misses cycle-99 lithium loss by 5.7% (Chen2020), 7.2% (OKane2022), 10.1% (NCA_Kim2011) and 7.0% (Ai2020), against 8.2, 5.9, 2.2 and 8.3% with the law's own lever and 1.1 to 8.0% with both inputs measured; it beats the law's lever on 15 of 40 designs. The capacity factor accelerates after cycle 10 on every set and the drift turns over, so straight lines cannot carry them. Milestone 5zp (what bends the law's line): fed the measured plating-weighted plating overpotential rise and the measured charge-capacity factor of 40 PyBaMM DFN designs, the ten-cycle forecast at αF/RT misses cycle-99 lithium loss by 1.4% (Chen2020) and 1.5% (OKane2022), against 3.8 and 3.4% with the measured OCP rise alone, and the line's bend falls from 0.10 and 0.09 to 0.03 and 0.04; either input alone does little, and on Ai2020 the overpotential doubles the bend (4.2 to 8.7%). A 10× finer table changes nothing. Diagnoses that read cycle 99, not forecasts. Milestone 5zo (lever or law): fed the measured plating-weighted anode OCP rise of 40 PyBaMM DFN designs, the forecast law at αF/RT with a ten-cycle line misses cycle-99 lithium loss by 3.8% (Chen2020), 3.4% (OKane2022), 1.2% (NCA_Kim2011) and 4.2% (Ai2020), against 8.2, 5.9, 2.2 and 8.3% with the law's own lever; the remainder is the law's line, whose R slope drifts 9 to 13% between early and late cycles. The node lever's OKane2022 over-read sits at the separator-side nodes, where the plating is (collector half's share 0.21). H209 supported, H210 inconclusive, H211 refuted. Milestone 5zn (where the plating lever should be read): on 40 PyBaMM DFN designs the plating sits 0.04 to 0.22 stoichiometry above the forecast law's window top; reading the law's lithium-to-stoichiometry shift at each node's cycle-2 stoichiometry reproduces the plating-weighted OCP rise with slope 1.00, 0.98, 0.84 and 1.18 by cycle 99 (the law's own lever needs 1.35 to 1.49 on LG M50), and on Chen2020 from cycle 10 (3.25 against 2.88 mV measured, 0.42 for the law). At αF/RT the ten-cycle forecast with it beats the law's on Ai2020 (8.3% to 2.3% error) and Chen2020 (8.2% to 5.9%) and loses on OKane2022 and NCA_Kim2011 (22 of 40 designs); H204 to H208 inconclusive. Milestone 5zm (how early the plating exponent can be read): cut at 10, 20 or 30 PyBaMM DFN cycles, 5zl's plating-weighted lever gives an exponent 2 to 3 times what LG M50 needs (100 and 49 to 75 against 38 and 34 at cycle 99), because the OCP where the plating sits rises several times faster than the law's lever while the law's window is on the graphite plateau; it is flat from cycle 10 on NCA_Kim2011 and settles by 30 on Ai2020. Early-exponent forecasts lose to αF/RT given the same cycles on 4 of 4 sets at 10 cycles and 3 of 4 at 30; fitting the law's line over 30 to 50 cycles at αF/RT halves the error or better on every set. Pre-registered: H200, H202 refuted, H201, H203 inconclusive. Milestone 5zl (what sets the plating exponent): on 40 PyBaMM DFN designs run to 100 cycles, αF/RT times the ratio of the plating-weighted end-of-charge OCP rise to the forecast law's own lever lands within 3 to 12% of the exponent the forecast needs on LG M50 and NCA_Kim2011, and 34% high on Ai2020; it beats the separator-node reading on 37 of 40 designs and cuts the 100-cycle forecast error threefold on LG M50 (a diagnosis: it reads cycle 99). It reverses 5zk's cross-pool reading. Pre-registered: H198, H199 supported, H195 to H197 inconclusive. Milestone 5zk (where the plating is): on 40 PyBaMM DFN designs run to 100 cycles, the separator-side node carries only 8 to 19% of a cycle's plating (plating-weighted depth 0.53 to 0.72 of the thickness), which explains why a separator-node rate index mis-tracked NCA_Kim2011's slowdown (0.28 in log). Read where the plating is, the potential lever shrinks to 0.64 of the separator node's on Ai2020 and 0.78 to 0.81 on LG M50: the implied exponent moves from 73 to 47 on Ai2020 (needed 21) and away from what Chen2020 and OKane2022 need. Pre-registered: H191, H192, H194 supported, H193 refuted. Milestone 5zj (where the lever goes): on PyBaMM's Ai2020 set, the intercalation overpotential and the charge-profile shape give back about 41% of the separator-surface OCP lever (about 20% on LG M50, −19% on NCA_Kim2011). That halves the exponent the lever implies there (73 to 43, against the 21 the forecast needs) but moves the other three sets further from theirs, so the plating exponent is not set at the separator node (post hoc, on 5z's committed records). A ten-cycle lithium ledger re-confirms 5p and 5za: Ai2020's loss is plating, which PyBaMM 26.10.1.1 books for one of its 34 parallel electrode pairs. The integrated side-reaction current matches the particles' loss to 0.01%, and a doubled mesh moves it by 0.1%. Milestone 5zh (calibration budget): resampling the 768 committed designs, a plating exponent calibrated on ten earlier 100-cycle runs matches the 160-run calibration in the median on all 24 pools (within 0.007), and ten runs from one earlier campaign do as well as scattered ones; but at the 90th percentile ten runs still lose to αF/RT on 10 of 24 pools (3 at 80 runs), and one run loses on all 24. H178 to H180 supported, H177 and H181 refuted; seen data only. Milestone 5zg (per-set plating exponent): calibrating the plating law's kinetic exponent once per parameter set, as the median oracle κ* over the set's earlier 100-cycle DFN runs, cuts the cycle-99 lithium-loss error on 128 fresh designs from 9.3% and 7.6% to 4.9% and 6.5% on LG M50 and improves both controls (5.6% to 4.9%, 1.7% to 0.9%); pre-registered H172 to H176 supported. Limits: 160 calibration runs per set, one current per set, modelled fade. Milestone 5zf (kinetic exponent): on 128 fresh designs (four sets, 100 DFN cycles, SEI + plating, seed 24) a per-design plating exponent κ estimated from cycles 2 to 10 forecasts the cycle-99 lithium loss worse than the physical αF/RT = 25.3 V−1 on all four pools (LG M50 0.127 and 0.122 against 0.099 and 0.059 median |ln err|); LG M50's potential lever rises under 1 mV in ten cycles, so κ is not identifiable there. The oracle κ that makes the forecast exact is 45 and 32 V−1 on LG M50 against 20 and 23 on Ai2020 and NCA_Kim2011: the law's lever is too shallow on LG M50. Modelled fade, one PyBaMM version. Milestone 5ze (overpotential diagnosis): on 128 fresh designs (four sets, 100 DFN cycles, SEI + plating, seed 23) 5zd's η-window law replicates on LG M50 (0.109 and 0.095 median |ln err| against 0.191 and 0.160 for 5zc) and keeps its Ai2020 cost (0.063 against 0.024). Feeding the law η's true drift to cycle 99 is worse on all four pools (Ai2020 0.111); a discharge/charge split of η from the ten-cycle discharge energy puts the charge side within 2 to 5 mV of the symmetric η and moves the error by at most 0.007. On 384 seen designs, extrapolating η's ten-cycle trend and choosing the reading per design also fail. So the remaining gap is in the law's structure. Modelled fade, one PyBaMM version. Milestone 5zd (consistent levers): reading the negative potential rise at the top of the η-shortened charge window, the same η 5zc measured from the charge Ah of cycles 2 to 10, cuts the cycle-99 lithium-loss error on fresh LG M50 pools (Chen2020, OKane2022, 64 designs, 100 DFN cycles, SEI + plating) from 0.202 and 0.167 to 0.104 and 0.064 median |ln err|, 59 of 64 designs won, with no new parameter; the separator-surface potential rise is forecast within 21 and 17 mV against 35 and 27 mV. NCA_Kim2011 improves (0.033 to 0.020), Ai2020 worsens (0.025 to 0.076) because its η drifts; rank correlation on LG M50 dips (0.97, 0.94). Modelled fade, one PyBaMM version. Milestone 5zc (loaded charge): replacing the open-circuit capacity in 5zb's kinetic law with the capacity between the cut-offs less an effective overpotential η, measured from each design's charge Ah in cycles 2 to 10, cuts the cycle-99 lithium-loss error on fresh LG M50 pools (Chen2020, OKane2022, 64 designs, 100 DFN cycles, SEI + plating) from 0.279 and 0.248 to 0.210 and 0.161 median |ln err|, winning on 64 of 64 designs, with Ai2020 0.030 and NCA_Kim2011 0.023 unchanged; a constant η predicts the cycle-99 charge Ah within 4 to 7%, against 20 to 86% for the open-circuit capacity. Post hoc, charge Ah plus the measured separator-surface potential rise make the LG M50 plating rate steady, so the surface rise is what is left to forecast. Modelled fade, one PyBaMM version. Milestone 5zb (kinetic law): with the plating per cycle proportional to the open-circuit charge capacity and slowed by the negative potential rise, the integrated loss is linear in the cycle count. A line fitted to cycles 2 to 10 forecasts the cycle-99 lithium loss on four fresh pools (128 designs, 100 DFN cycles, SEI + plating, new currents) better than the earlier power law on every pool and on 122 of 128 designs: Ai2020 0.076 against 0.150 median |ln err|, NCA_Kim2011 0.024 against 0.078, LG M50 0.24 to 0.26 against 0.31 to 0.33, ranks 0.98 to 0.999. The LG M50 residual matches the loaded charge shrinking faster than the open-circuit capacity says. Modelled fade, one PyBaMM version. Milestone 5za (surface feedback): on two fresh LG M50 pools (Chen2020, OKane2022, 64 designs, 100 DFN cycles with SEI + plating) the ten-cycle forecast with the plating feedback read at the separator-side particle surface over-predicts the cycle-99 lithium loss by 21 to 23% against 35% for the open-circuit reading, no constant fitted, ranking kept (Spearman 0.96); it misses the 15% bar and does harm on NCA_Kim2011 and Ai2020, where it predicts the surface rise exactly yet errs more, so the open-circuit predictor works there partly by compensation. Ai2020's unbooked lithium is PyBaMM's side-reaction totals omitting its 34 parallel electrodes (5p); corrected, plating is 99.6%. Limits: one current, offset from cycles 2 to 10, modelled fade. Milestone 5z (mechanism): on 24 re-run LG M50 designs (Chen2020, OKane2022, 100 DFN cycles with SEI + plating) the per-cycle plating falls about 3.3× from cycle 2 to 99 because the negative electrode's open-circuit potential at the separator-side particle surface rises 38 mV at end of charge, where the open-circuit window used by milestone 5x moves only 0.5 to 9 mV; the same term carries the slowdown on NCA_Kim2011. Plating is 99.8% of the lost lithium there, and a one-node rate index tracks the plating change within 0.015 log units. (5z's note that only 3% of Ai2020's loss is booked is the parallel-electrode count; 5za.) Limits: seen designs, one node, modelled fade. Milestone 5y (fresh pools): on 192 new designs run 100 DFN cycles, the plating feedback exp(−αFΔU/RT), with no fitted constant and one power law fitted to the feedback-free loss on every pool, brings the cycle-99 lithium loss to within 2.4% and 3.8% on two NCA_Kim2011 pools and 10.2% on Ai2020 (uncorrected law 31%, 30%, 18%) and removes 5x's double count on Ai2020. Its energy ranking beats an 8-run calibration on NCA_Kim2011 (Spearman 0.82, 0.93 against 0.62, 0.84) but trails 5x's uniformly biased forecast on Ai2020 (0.875 against 0.974), and raw cycle-10 energy ranks at 0.93 to 0.96 on all three pools. Limits: two cell sets, the law form chosen on seen pools, SEI treated as plating, OKane2022's plating parameters, modelled fade. Milestone 5x (deriving the correction): PyBaMM's irreversible plating rate falls as exp(−αFΔU/RT) when lost lithium raises the negative electrode's potential at top of charge (α = 0.65). Applied to the first ten DFN cycles with no fitted constant, it brings the cycle-99 lithium loss on two NCA_Kim2011 pools to within 5.6% and 3.1% of DFN (ten-cycle law 27%, 30%) and ranks 100-cycle energy at 0.69 and 0.91, above 5w's 8-run calibration (0.51, 0.76). Over ten committed pools (622 designs) it orders the fitted slopes correctly (Spearman 0.92) and beats the √cycle energy fit on 10 of 10, but under-predicts Ai2020's loss by about 27% (the √n law already bends) and gives no feedback on the LG M50 sets, whose graphite sits on its plateau. Pools seen in aggregate; SEI treated as plating. Milestone 5w (the correction on other cells): on fresh NCA_Kim2011, Chen2020 and OKane2022 pools (192 designs, 100 DFN cycles each, 56 held out per pool) the balance map fed the ten-cycle lithium law with 5v's self-limiting correction, its intercept recalibrated on 8 designs and its slope kept from Ai2020, ranks the 100-cycle energy at Spearman 0.76, 0.94 and 0.94, against −0.42, 0.80 and 0.80 for 5n's √cycle energy fit (beats it in 149 of 150 calibration draws). The slope is cell-specific (0.34 to 0.37 on the two LG M50 sets, 0.58 on Ai2020), so the cycle-99 lithium loss is off by a median 8.5% there, and on these pools raw cycle-10 energy already ranks at 0.93 to 0.96, so they do not test the screen. Modelled fade (PyBaMM 26.10.1.1, OKane2022's plating parameters on every set), not measured cells. Milestone 5v (a self-limiting correction, fresh pools): on 5u's committed pools the ten-cycle lithium law already ranks the cycle-99 DFN loss at Spearman 0.98 to 0.99, but the balance map is ill-conditioned (a 10% random error on the true loss drops its energy ranking from 0.96 to 0.38 to 0.67) and the law's size error grows with the fraction of lithium lost. One line, ln(Llaw/LDFN) = 0.658 + 0.577 ln(Llaw/nLi), fitted on 5u's three Ai2020 pools and frozen, was pre-registered on three fresh Ai2020 pools (64 Sobol designs each, seed 15; 192 DFN runs to cycle 100, 189 scored). The corrected map ranks the 100-cycle energy at 0.92, 0.96 and 0.96 (5n's √cycle energy fit 0.67, 0.62, 0.59; uncorrected 0.61, 0.68, 0.82; fed DFN's own loss 0.96 to 0.97), gets the cycle-99 loss to a median 4% (uncorrected 11 to 18%), and with the raw top 4 finds the DFN best on every pool at 6.3 resumed designs against 7.7 for 5n's union. Refitted on 8 designs per pool the constants barely move (A 0.61 to 0.72, S 0.57 to 0.60). Limits: one cell set, the one the constants came from; empirical, no mechanism fitted; three pools. Milestone 5u (fresh pools, a per-pool loss law): the lithium-loss law picked per pool from the median ten-cycle power-law exponent (≥ 0.6: a + b√n, else a nb), then 5s's map, pre-registered on four pools no milestone had run (64 Sobol designs each, seed 14; 256 DFN runs to cycle 100, 241 scored). The selector picked as predicted, and the median predicted cycle-99 lithium loss was 1.05, 0.99 and 0.94 of DFN's on Ai2020 0.3×, 0.4× and 0.5× (1.32 on NCA_Kim2011@0.625×). Fed DFN's own cycle-99 loss the map ranks the 100-cycle energy at Spearman 0.95 to 0.97 on all four pools. Fed the fitted law it ranks better than 5n's √cycle energy fit on only 1 of 4 (0.64 to 0.76 on Ai2020), predicts fade size better on 1 of 4, and as the union's fade list misses the DFN best by 1.25% on one pool where 5n's union is exact (5n's misses by 0.87% on another). Per-design lithium ratios run from about 0.8 to 1.45 of the truth: the map is right, the pool law is right on the median, and the per-design ten-cycle fit is what loses the ranking. 5n's union stays the procedure. Milestone 5t (a slowing lithium-loss law): 5s's map fed L(n) = a + b√n, fitted to the same ten DFN cycles and chosen on lithium alone from 27 designs run to cycle 100, scored pre-registered on the 13 committed pools those designs did not come from (no new simulation). It ranks the 100-cycle DFN energy better than 5s's power-law map on 12 of 13 (sign test p = 0.003) and better than 5n's √cycle energy fit on 8 of 13 (bar 9, mixed; by 0.23 to 0.33 on Ai2020@0.625×, Chen2020@2× and OKane2022@2×, worse on both NCA_Kim2011 pools); its fade size is worse on 7 of 13; and as the union screen's fade list it misses the DFN best by up to 3.2% where 5n's union is within 0.16%. 5n's union stays the procedure. Milestone 5s (balance map as a fade predictor): 5r's electrode-balance map fed a power law L(n) = a nb through each design's lithium loss over ten DFN cycles, read at cycle 99. Pre-registered on 17 committed 100-cycle pools (1,108 fresh ten-cycle DFN runs, which reproduce the committed energies exactly): it ranks the 100-cycle DFN energy better than 5n's √cycle energy fit on 2 of 17 conditions, predicts fade size better on 7 (none of the eight Ai2020 pools), and as the union screen's fade list misses the DFN best by up to 6.9% where 5n's union is within 0.32% (all four hypotheses refuted). Post hoc, on 27 designs run to cycle 100: fed DFN's own cycle-99 lithium loss the map is within a mean 0.02 to 0.05 of the fade on Ai2020, Chen2020 and NCA_Kim2011 (0.12 on OKane2022); the power law over-predicts that loss 1.2 to 2.8 times because plating's growth exponent falls from about 0.85 over cycles 2 to 10 to 0.24 to 0.63 by cycles 50 to 99. The balance map works; a cheap fade predictor needs a self-limiting lithium-loss law. Milestone 5r (electrode balance): a map from the parameter set and the design alone (both electrodes’ lithium capacities, the cyclable lithium and the two OCP curves; the open-circuit window between the cut-offs and its energy) turns each DFN run’s own lithium loss into its energy fade with no fitted constant. Pre-registered on 128 fresh DFN runs (8 conditions, 8 new designs each, 20 cycles with and without degradation): within 0.05 of the degradation-added fade on 34 of 40 fading designs, mean error 0.038 against 0.053 for the best constant fade per lithium, a within-pool ranking at least as good as the lithium share on all 5 fading conditions (Ai2020@0.3× +0.95 against +0.48, @1× +0.81 against +0.21), and errors concentrated on designs far from open circuit (Spearman −0.73; NCA_Kim2011 over-predicted by up to 0.24). Fade splits into a design-only map and a lithium-loss rate; the map is fed DFN’s own loss, so it is a decomposition, not yet a predictor. Milestone 5q (a two-cycle plating predictor): two SPMe cycles with SEI and plating on all 2,324 committed designs of 36 conditions, tested on the 24 conditions not read before the plan. The cycle-2 plating rate does not rank the 100-cycle DFN fade (median Spearman 0.03); a self-limited plating correction ranks designs worse than SPMe’s plain cycle-2 energy on 20 of 24; a top-half cut before the union screen missed by up to 6.1% and cost more than the screen it was meant to shorten; SPMe failed on 456 designs, the DFN best among them on 7 pools. Energy lost per unit of lithium lost varies about twofold within a pool, so a fade predictor needs an electrode-balance map. Milestone 5p (what makes the designs fade): an ablation of PyBaMM's two degradation options on 8 committed conditions (128 DFN runs, 20 cycles). On the five that fade by 5 to 25%, the irreversible-plating submodel alone reproduces 0.998 to 1.015 of the fade and solvent-diffusion SEI alone 0.000 to 0.006; a closed form of PyBaMM's SEI law matches its lithium loss to under 10−4. PyBaMM 26.10.1.1's side-reaction lithium-loss variables under-count by the parallel-electrode count (34 on Ai2020, all 93 degraded runs). No earlier score changes; the programme's fade is OKane2022's plating kinetics, copied to six of seven sets. Milestone 5o (a salt floor before any simulation): drop every design whose closed-form salt number rkt (0.04 s per design) is below −0.2, then run 5n's union screen on the rest. Pre-registered on three fresh pools (192 PyBaMM runs, NCA_Kim2011@0.875×, Chen2020@1.75×, Ai2020@0.875×): it dropped 25 to 35 of 64 designs, returned the pool's DFN best on all three, and took 0.48 to 0.79 of the union screen's time (0.15 to 0.20 of all-DFN). The best design's rkt was never below −0.08 on 36 pools; a floor at 0 would have missed by 9.3%. The (energy, rkt) Pareto front is the wrong cut: on fade-limited Ai2020 the best sits on layers 4 to 7 and a 3-layer cut misses by up to 4.7%. Milestone 5n (late fade from ten cycles): DFN to cycle 10 on every design, a least-squares line in √cycle through cycles 5 to 10 read at cycle 100, and the top 4 by that extrapolation together with the top 4 by raw cycle-10 energy resumed to cycle 100. Pre-registered on three fresh pools (192 PyBaMM runs, Ai2020@0.275× and @0.35×, NCA_Kim2011@1.25×): within 0.16% of the pool's DFN best on all three, where the raw 10-cycle screen missed by 9.2% and 3.9%; the extrapolation lifted the low-current Ai2020 ranking from Spearman 0.10 and 0.48 to 0.57 and 0.63, and is anti-correlated on NCA_Kim2011 (−0.68), where the raw list carries the pool; wall time 0.24 to 0.32 of all-DFN (bar 0.30, mixed); against 5m's ladder 0.16% worse on one pool, 0.39% better on another. Over 33 conditions the union is exact on 29, worst 0.32%.

Milestone 5m (successive halving over resumed runs): DFN to cycle 10 on every design, then the top 16 resumed to 20, the top 8 to 50 and the top 3 to 100. Resuming (PyBaMM starting_solution, 10-cycle chunks) reproduces uninterrupted runs bit for bit on 23 designs at 0.85 to 0.97 of their time. Pre-registered on three fresh pools (216 PyBaMM runs, Ai2020@0.3× and @0.4375×, Ecker2015@0.75×): exact on two, 2.7% short on Ai2020@0.3× where the 10-cycle screen missed by 8.8%, at 0.24 to 0.29 of all-DFN’s wall time (a run’s first ten cycles cost 15 to 17% of it). There the best design ranks 28th of 53 at cycle 10 and first only at cycle 50: designs that start best fade fastest. Milestone 5l (retention from a short run): of the three factors of the 100-cycle score (thermodynamic energy, utilisation, retention), only retention needs simulation, and ten DFN cycles carry it. Pre-registered on three fresh pools (384 PyBaMM runs, Ai2020@0.625×, NCA_Kim2011@0.75×, OKane2022@1.75×): cycle-10 Wh/kg ranks cycle-100 Wh/kg at Spearman 0.92 to 0.97, and DFN@10 on all designs plus DFN@100 on the top 3 returned the DFN best on all three at 0.19 of all-DFN’s wall time; a sqrt-cycle fade extrapolation ranks worse. Known failure (development): Ai2020 at 0.25× and 0.375×, missed by 6 to 7%. Milestone 5j (salt pre-screen in the search) runs DFN, not SPMe, on every design whose closed-form salt ratio rkt is at most 0.10, and keeps the trust rule and band stop for the rest. Pre-registered on two fresh pools (256 PyBaMM runs, OKane2022 at 1.25× and Chen2020 at 1.5× current): it returned the DFN-best design on both, at 1.12× and 0.90× the earlier procedure’s wall time (median 1.01× over 19 committed conditions), so it is not a saving. It is a fix: on Chen2020@1.5× the earlier procedure stopped verifying inside the flagged block, one design short of the best (SPMe 19% low), and missed it by 4.5%. The best design’s rkt lay between −0.06 and +0.58 on all 21 conditions and below the flag on 8; discarding flagged designs would have missed by up to 17%, and a thermodynamic energy bound (never violated over 1,395 designs) prunes none of 429 flagged ones. Limits: two fresh conditions on graphite cells seen at other currents, one machine’s timings. Milestone 5i (closed-form trust flag) derives SPMe’s minimum salt ratio from the parameter set and the design alone: the steady electrolyte profile under SPMe’s uniform reaction, with concentration-dependent diffusivity handled exactly by the Kirchhoff transform. Pre-registered on the constant-diffusivity form over 1,280 committed designs (19 cell–current conditions): it ranks designs as SPMe does (Spearman 0.99) and predicts SPMe’s mis-scoring as well as the simulated flag (AUC 0.951 against 0.957), but over-predicts depletion (H66 mixed). The De(c) form, registered before 816 fresh PyBaMM runs were read, misclassifies 0 of 408 fresh designs (mean error 0.0003). It models SPMe’s electrolyte, not DFN’s (mean difference 0.03). Milestone 6a (measured cells) checks SPM, SPMe and DFN against the measured constant-current discharges PyBaMM ships for the Kokam cell of Ecker et al. (2015, 1C and 5C) and the Enertech pouch of Ai et al. (2020, 0.1C to 2C). Pre-registered: SPMe is never closer to the measured capacity than DFN by more than 0.13 points (H61 supported); where SPMe’s r_min is at least 0.5 the two agree within 0.06% while both miss the cell by 0.9 to 4.3% (H63 supported); r_min does not order the SPMe–DFN gap across the two cells (Spearman −0.14, H62 mixed). After the verdicts: the Ai cell’s logged temperature rise (1.6, 4.0, 10.4 K) matches PyBaMM’s lumped thermal model within 0.1 K; with heating the 2C SPMe–DFN gap falls from 1.50 to 0.32 points, and DFN’s 18.6 mV isothermal fit is heating error cancelling a 4% capacity offset. Default mesh, two cells, discharge only; no measured curve reaches the salt-starved designs where SPMe fails. Milestone 5h (a gap-aware answer step) targets 5g's one miss: on Ai2020 at half current SPMe scored nearly every sound design about 24% low, so the answer step stopped 3.2% short of the DFN best. The band stop keeps verifying with DFN while some unverified design's SPMe score times q (the median DFN/SPMe ratio over verified designs with r_min > 0.1, floored at 1) could beat the verified best. Chosen on the 13 committed conditions, it was pre-registered and run on six new ones with fresh designs (788 PyBaMM runs: Ai2020 at 0.75× and 0.25×, NCA_Kim2011, Chen2020 and Ecker2015 at 0.5×, OKane2022 at 1.5×). It returned the DFN best on all six at 0.33 to 1.07 of all-DFN wall time; 5g's iterate step did too, including Ai2020 at 0.75× where SPMe is 24% low (H58 refuted), so the band stop's extra 9 and 11 DFN runs on the Ai2020 pools bought nothing here. Over 19 conditions the iterate step misses on one (3.2%), the band stop on none. Rule recall stayed at or above 0.97; 13 Ai2020 DFN runs at 0.25× failed in the first cycle and were dropped. One PyBaMM version, 64 designs per condition, current the only condition varied. Milestone 5g (skip SPMe or not, at new currents) pre-registers a gate that reads the first 8 SPMe runs of a pool and skips SPMe (running DFN on every design) when 4 or more fail or deplete their salt (r_min ≤ 0.1), and otherwise runs the 5e rule with an answer step that keeps verifying the merged leader. It runs on 64 fresh designs at six conditions no run had used (768 PyBaMM runs): OKane2022, Chen2020, Marquis2019, Ecker2015 and Mohtat2020 at twice the areal current density, Ai2020 at half. Current moves the suspect share on every cell (Chen2020 0.25 to 0.81, Ecker2015 0.06 to 0.70, OKane2022 0.18 to 0.81, Ai2020 0.72 to 0.31 at half current). The gate chooses the cheaper branch on 4 of 6 (refuted): a structural SPMe failure costs under a second, so pools full of failures make SPMe cheap; the gated cost stays within 1.13× of the cheaper branch. The rule finds every mis-scored design at every condition. The answer is the DFN best on five conditions and 3.2% short on Ai2020 at half current, where SPMe scores designs a median 24% low and the best one is never verified (refuted). After the verdicts, a gate that also uses the SPMe-to-DFN time ratio from one DFN run is right on 12 of 13 conditions. Milestone 5f (a pilot switch and a verified answer step) tests, on 64 fresh designs on each of Mohtat2020, Ai2020, NCA_Kim2011 and Ecker2015 (515 runs), whether 8 SPMe runs plus 2 DFN runs can tell when to skip SPMe and run DFN on everything, and whether verifying the leading design until it is DFN-scored returns the DFN best. The answer step does, in all 120 replayed trials; all 3 early SPMe stops re-solve at tight tolerance to within 0.2% of DFN; recall stays 1.00. The switch fails its test: on Ai2020, where all-DFN is 11.6% cheaper, it fires in 20% of trials, because a salt cut-off of 0.10 misses mis-scored designs with minimum salt ratio up to 0.32. Across 11 cell pools the rule never costs more than 12% over all-DFN and saves 49 to 64% on six, so the recommendation is to run the rule every time. The switch constants were chosen on a post hoc replay of the seven committed cells. Milestone 5e (the rule on new cells) fixes in advance the two-part rule from 5c and 5d (re-solve early SPMe stops at tight tolerance; DFN-verify failed runs, then the rest in ascending minimum salt ratio, until three sound) and runs it on 64 fresh designs on each of two cells it was not built on, Marquis2019 and Chen2020 (256 runs). On Chen2020 it verifies all 9 mis-scored designs in 15 DFN runs (23% of the pool), among them the DFN-best design, which SPMe scores 23% low and ranks 16th; Marquis2019 has no mis-scored design and costs 4 runs. The planned answer step lands 1.3% below the DFN best on Marquis2019 because it compares verified DFN scores with SPMe scores that run 1 to 6% high at the top; taking the best verified design instead (chosen after the verdicts) reaches the DFN best on both cells. No run stopped early, so the re-solve step is untested. Milestone 5d (why SPMe fails) re-solves, pre-registered, every SPMe run on the committed benches that failed outright (61: NCA_Kim2011 49, OKane2022 12) or stopped early (6, Mohtat2020) under four solver and mesh variants, with 24 completed runs as controls (455 runs). Tight tolerances (rtol 1e-6, atol 1e-8, IDAKLU or CasADi) finish all 6 early stops, which then score within 0.3% of DFN; more Newton iterations finish none. No setting gives any of the 61 outright failures a usable score: in 59 SPMe’s linearised salt concentration goes below zero in the first discharge (median −8% of initial), the charge step has no valid start, and PyBaMM discards the run. So stops are re-solved, failures go to DFN. All four hypotheses supported; V0 reproduces all 91 committed runs. Milestone 5c (setting the cut-off on a new cell) compares, pre-registered, a trust-flag cut-off fitted to 8 random DFN runs with verifying designs in ascending order of SPMe’s minimum salt ratio until three sound ones in a row, on the three earlier cells and two new PyBaMM cells, Mohtat2020 and NCA_Kim2011 (64 Sobol designs each, 256 runs). On Mohtat2020 both fail (recall 0.00 and 0.17; H33, H34 and H37 refuted): its 6 mis-scored designs are SPMe runs whose solver stopped part-way (cycles 3 to 90), returned by PyBaMM as normal solutions, with no salt depletion. Among SPMe runs that finish, r_min ranks the mis-scored designs at AUC 0.995 or better on every cell that has any. Flagging early stops as well (post hoc), bottom-up verification finds every mis-scored design on all five cells with 16%, 95%, 6%, 14% and 88% of the pool sent to DFN (mis-scored shares 13%, 89%, 2%, 9%, 81%), always fewer than the 8-run calibration (23% to 98%). Milestone 5b (transfer) runs the trust flag and 9 frozen search methods, pre-registered, on two more PyBaMM parameter sets, Ecker2015 and Ai2020 (64 Sobol designs each, 384 runs, current scaled to the same areal density). SPMe's minimum salt ratio ranks the designs it mis-scores at AUC 0.995 on Ai2020 (57 of 64 mis-scored), but the OKane2022 cut-off r ≤ 0.07 misclassifies 20.3% there (best cut-off 0.33; H2 refuted); SPMe@10 no longer ranks DFN better than SPMe@100 (−0.01 and −0.11); the methods' ordering transfers (Spearman 0.73, 0.70), and the 2-cycle SPMe and DFN screens stay within 1.3× of the fastest method on all three cells while GP-EI is 1.9 to 3.7×. Cells are design-space variants (5% inactive rule, borrowed degradation parameters), not the published cells. Milestone 5a (fresh designs) re-tests, unchanged and pre-registered, the post-hoc winners of parts 2b and 4b on 128 new Sobol designs (384 PyBaMM runs, same parameter set). On pools of 64 the whole-pool 10-cycle SPMe screen reaches a design within 1% of the DFN best in 122.9 s against GP-EI's 220.4 s and the SPM@2 screen's 205.0 s (both p < 0.001); SPMe@10 ranks 100-cycle DFN at Spearman 0.668 against 0.575 for SPMe@100; the 15 methods' medians correlate at 0.924 across the two design sets. Cheap-start MF-UCB co-kriging beats GP-EI at every pool size but is 1.36× and 1.71× the best screen at 16 and 32 designs (refuted), and is fastest at 96. A 2- or 10-cycle SPMe screen stays within 1.4× of the fastest method at every pool size on both sets (descriptive). Same parameter set and protocol: transfer to other cells is untested. Milestone 3 part 2b (where SPMe errs) models SPMe's residual against 100-cycle DFN as a function of SPMe's own minimum salt ratio r. The registered form -ln r, from the log in SPMe's electrolyte overpotential, halves the cross-validated error (21.3 to 11.3 Wh/kg) and beats (1 − r)2 and the 0.1 flag. As a planner, fitted on 16-design pilots, it lands within 2× of SPMe's DFN cost on only 2 of 4 cycle counts. As an online correction it is slower than milestone 1's flag rule (528 against 418 s). Post hoc: SPMe@100's 14-call cost comes from the single DFN-best design, which is salt-depleted and drops from rank 1 at 10 cycles to 41 at 100. A plain whole-pool 10-cycle SPMe screen reaches a design within 1% of the DFN best in 123 s on pools of 64 and 172 s on 96, ahead of GP-EI (220 s) and every earlier screen. Exploratory: one parameter set, the same 128 designs. A research programme (proposal and log on the project page) on when a lithium-ion electrode design search can trust a reduced electrochemical model. Milestone 4b (co-kriging multi-fidelity BO) replays autoregressive co-kriging over a cheap rung (SPM or 2-cycle DFN) and 100-cycle DFN, with augmented EI (Huang et al. 2006) and an MF-UCB fidelity rule (after Kandasamy et al. 2016), on the cached benchmark with measured run times. Started from five random DFN runs (122 s), no planned variant beats GP-EI (best 204.6 against 220.4 s on pools of 64; 267.1 against 220.4 s on 96) and all are far slower than whole-pool screening on small pools (157 against 46 s at 16 designs); three pre-registered hypotheses, two refuted. Charging each design its own measured time keeps the method order (Spearman 0.90). Exploratory, chosen after the result: starting from ten 2-cycle DFN runs ties the best screen at every pool size (38, 90, 144, 174 s at 16, 32, 64, 96 designs) and beats GP-EI at each. Milestone 3 (theory, part 2a) treats the screen’s residual as independent noise and gives an exact expected count of DFN runs (a one-dimensional integral for Gaussian noise). As a planner it calls whether whole-pool screening beats GP-EI right on 14 of 16 (screen, pool size) cases, against 8 of 16 for the worst-case formula; with one whole-space noise level it ranks the 11 screens only at Spearman 0.51 (refuted), 0.86 with the noise level near the top, because SPMe’s large errors fall on particular designs (on the DFN-best ones at 100 cycles: 14 DFN runs needed, 3 predicted). Milestone 3 (theory, part 1) proves that screen-then-verify needs at most as many full DFN runs as there are designs within 2κ of the best, where κ is the screen’s worst residual after the best affine fit, so scale and shift errors are free; the bound held on all 330 (screen, pool) cases. Across 11 screens κ ranks the DFN calls needed at Spearman 0.72, the raw error at −0.07; SPM’s residual is a quarter of SPMe’s (11.0 against 42.8 Wh/kg) and SPMe’s tracks its own minimum salt concentration (Spearman −0.82). The worst-case cost formula built on it predicted screen against GP-EI on only 8 of 16 pool sizes (refuted). Milestone 4 (search replay) replays 12 search methods on the cached benchmark, 30 pools of 64 designs, each simulation charged its measured wall time: screening every candidate with the plain SPM (100 cycles) or a 2-cycle DFN run and verifying in screen order reaches a design within 1% of the best 100-cycle DFN score in a median 153 or 160 s, against 220 s for GP-EI on DFN; the 10-cycle DFN screen takes 253 s (pre-registered H7, that it would need a third of GP-EI's time, refuted), successive halving over DFN cycles 247 s (185 s if runs resume), and milestone 1's trust flag cuts SPMe screening from 700 to 418 s. On pools of 96 GP-EI catches up, so whole-pool screening suits small candidate sets. Milestone 2 (dense benchmark) runs 128 fresh space-filling (Sobol) designs for 100 cycles under SPM, SPMe and DFN (384 runs, every cycle kept): a 10-cycle DFN run ranks the designs by their 100-cycle DFN Wh/kg at Spearman 0.962 (95% 0.932–0.977), against 0.641 (0.480–0.789) for a full 100-cycle SPMe run, at the same wall time (3.6 s against 3.7 s), and its top 10 contain the DFN-best design, which SPMe ranks 41st. Unplanned: the plain SPM ranks better than SPMe (0.955; 0.984 against 0.769 over the 121 designs SPMe completes), though it over-scores the best design by 20 Wh/kg, and 15 of 128 designs (12%) are mis-scored by SPMe by over 25%. Milestone 2a, the same question on the 49 stratified designs of energy-cell-dfn: 10-cycle DFN 0.977 against 0.834 for 100-cycle SPMe (paired bootstrap difference 0.138, 95% 0.057–0.271), and a linear fade extrapolation fails (Spearman 0.01). Milestone 1: a 2-cycle SPMe run's minimum electrolyte concentration classifies the designs SPMe under-scores by more than 25% with ROC AUC 0.997 on the 49 (0.994 on the 128, whole-run minimum). Re-runs reproduce the committed SPMe and DFN scores exactly. Limits: one parameter set and protocol, costs timed on one design and one 4-core machine, no measured cell for these designs.
